symptom.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by a major depressive episode accompanied by delusions and/or hallucinations that are typically mood-congruent, such as themes of guilt, worthlessness, or impending catastrophe. Clinically, it often presents with pervasive low mood or loss of interest, marked functional decline, and psychotic experiences that emerge as the depression deepens, sometimes leading to high suicide risk or severe impairment in self-care and social/occupational functioning. The course may be episodic, but psychotic features usually appear only during the most severe phases of depression and resolve as mood improves, helping distinguish it from primary psychotic disorders like schizophrenia. Careful assessment is needed to differentiate it from bipolar depression, schizoaffective disorder, and non-psychotic major depression, as treatment commonly requires a combination of antidepressant and antipsychotic medication, and sometimes electroconvulsive therapy in severe or refractory cases.

patient.stressor: About six months before presentation, Ruth was promoted to a lead role in casino surveillance after a longtime supervisor retired, which meant longer night shifts, more responsibility for incident review, and pressure from management to cut down on losses. Initially she treated it like another challenge, juggling the new hours with her softball league and salsa classes, but over time she began dropping out of social activities and spending most of her off-hours alone in her apartment reviewing footage on her laptop. Around four months before seeking care, after a high-profile cheating investigation in which she worried she had missed key cues, she became increasingly preoccupied with the idea that the cameras were somehow "watching her back" even when she was off duty and that mistakes she’d made in the past were being silently recorded and judged, which eroded her confidence and made it harder to function on the casino floor. Coworkers noticed she was no longer her outgoing self and that she seemed fearful in the control room; she finally agreed to see a psychiatrist after her manager sent her home mid-shift when she became visibly distressed and insisted that security footage was being used to prove she was a danger to other staff.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve messed everything up at work and that everyone can see how worthless I am, like it’s all being recorded as proof.”

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: I keep hearing this low, male voice when I’m alone in my apartment or in the control room on breaks, and it whispers things like, “We’ve got it all on camera, everyone knows what you did,” and it sounds so real that I catch myself looking around for a speaker or someone hiding even though I know that doesn’t make sense.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up feeling like there’s a weight sitting on my chest and this heavy, gray sadness that doesn’t lift even when something good happens, like a coworker cracking a joke or my sister calling to check in.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to love playing softball and going to salsa after my shifts, but now even the thought of putting on my shoes to go out feels pointless, so I just cancel on people and sit on the couch replaying casino footage or staring at the wall.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: My body feels like it’s moving through molasses—at work I catch myself just sitting there, staring at the monitors with my hands frozen on the keyboard, and when someone asks me a question it takes me a long time to answer because my mouth and my thoughts feel so slow.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how much I sleep during the day after a night shift, I still feel completely drained, like walking from my bed to the kitchen or standing through a short staff briefing is enough to wipe me out.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I’m convinced I’m the worst person on the team, like every tiny mistake I’ve ever made is stored on some hidden server and they’re compiling it all to prove I’m dangerous and incompetent, and I lie awake replaying years of footage in my head and telling myself I deserve to be fired or worse for letting everyone down.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: Lately I keep thinking it would be better for everyone if I just disappeared, and on the drive home from the casino I catch myself picturing turning the wheel into the concrete barrier or just not waking up after my shift, and those thoughts feel more like plans than passing ideas.

add_requirements.delusions_and_hallucinations_occur_exclu: I never had these thoughts about secret footage or heard this whispering voice until after I sank into this heavy depression a few months ago, and on the rare days when my mood lightens a bit, the voice and the feeling that everything is being recorded against me also fade into the background.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve been calling out of shifts, getting written up for missing incidents on the monitors, and I’ve basically stopped seeing friends or going to softball or salsa, spending most of my time alone at home feeling too overwhelmed and ashamed to do anything but sit and stare.
add_requirements.duration: This whole stretch of feeling deeply down, exhausted, and haunted by the idea that my mistakes are being watched and judged has been going on for about four months, ever since that big cheating investigation at work.
